content:
nina: Quick sync - we merged the tenant-priority weight change yesterday. Seeing unexpected churn in cross-region routing for small tenants.

cesar: The change made priority_weights multiplicative with cost_score. Tiny tenants suddenly look cheaper to route to distant cheaper shards.

ben: Why multiplicative vs additive? We need to discuss the math - additive keeps interpretability. Multiplicative compounds effects.

nina: We did multiplicative to let priority sway decisions more strongly. But maybe we over-weighted it.

cesar: Proposed fix: normalize priority to a bounded influence using softmax over tenant_priority_scores before combining with cost. That keeps relative ordering but limits absolute swing.

ben: Example pipeline: p = softmax(alpha * priority_raw); final_score = w_cost*cost_score + w_latency*lat_score + w_priority*p; Alpha controls sharpness. Default alpha=0.8.

monitor-bot: alert: cross_region_routing_increase for small_tenants > 10% over baseline in the last 30m.

nina: Ops mitigation: reduce priority weight to 0.1 for small tenants via runtime override. We should still fix math though.

qa-bot: test failures: ranker_integration_test flakiness increased - likely due to non-deterministic softmax when alpha high. Need stable sorting ties. Add epsilon tie-breaker by tenant id.

cesar: Back-of-envelope: softmax keeps interpretable bounds [0,1] and avoids multiplicative runaway. Will open RFC to change scoring to use bounded priority.

ben: Also add a gating param 'priority_mode' = {additive, bounded_softmax, multiplicative} so we can A/B test safely. Default to bounded_softmax after rollout.

nina: Action items: cesar to prototype bounded_softmax, qa to add deterministic sort tie-breaker, infra to add runtime toggle for priority_mode. We'll canary and monitor price/latency.

ben: One more: document tradeoffs clearly - multiplicative can amplify small priority differences which is good for premium tenants but risky for long tail. Add that to RFC.

nina: OK. Closing for now - RFC soon.
